title: Admin intake — caseflow & prioritization matrix for enterprise RBAC/SSO/SCIM requests
creator: Lina Gómez
description: Create a reproducible intake caseflow and prioritization matrix for non-bug enterprise admin & access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning gaps, org policy exceptions). Goal: standardize decisioning across Sales/Support/SEs/Security so we can route, quantify, and commit SLAs for enterprise customers needing admin-level changes or integrations. The deliverable will include: a scoring rubric (impact, security risk, compliance, implementation complexity, account tier), a service-level matrix (Triage/Response/ETA), and explicit escalation routes (self-serve, SE-assisted, security review, legal/contract).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A prioritized matrix that maps score bands to routing+SLA (e.g., score 0-4 self-serve, 5-8 SE-assisted within 3 business days, 9+ security/legal + enterprise SLA).
2) A decision flow diagram for intake owners (Support, AE, SE, CSM) with terminal actions and required artifacts (audit request, customer justification, signed DPA/SoA where needed).
3) Templates for intake form fields and minimum evidence (customer tenant ID, org admin contact, requested RBAC change, justification, requested time window).
4) Linked Confluence page and triage dashboard filter in Looker/Metabase.
5) Pilot with two enterprise customers and measure routing accuracy and time-to-first-response improvement by >=30%.
scope: In scope: intake for policy/access changes, RBAC role additions/removals, SSO/SAML onboarding failures requiring dev work, SCIM provisioning gaps, temporary org policy exceptions. Out of scope: bug fixes in runtime, quota increases that are purely billing, feature requests that require product design and roadmap prioritization.
proposed_rubric: Columns: impact_on_data_sensitivity (0-4), operational_disruption (0-4), compliance_requirement (0-4), implementation_complexity (0-4), customer_tier_weight (0-2). Score = sum * weight rules. Routing thresholds: 0-6 (Self-serve + Docs), 7-10 (SE-assisted, standard SLA), 11-14 (Security review + technical implementation), 15+ (Legal/Contracts + exec escalation). Example: RBAC request to add reviewer role for a low-tier customer that affects no sensitive data = score 3 -> self-serve or SE assist; SAML onboarding for large enterprise with SCIM mapping gaps and PII field mapping = score 13 -> security review + prioritized queue.
decision_notes:
Trade-offs discussed: keep rubric small to avoid overfitting vs. add more signal (cost: more fields increases friction). We favored fewer core signals to ensure form completion rate. Consider dynamic follow-up questions after initial score to collect deeper evidence for high-risk cases.
Routing trade-off: route conservative (more security reviews) initially to reduce incidents, then loosen thresholds post-pilot once confidence grows.
